solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Find a way round team with pace

parts.note: a side is a team, as in a football side
a step is a single pace in walking

explanation.surface: A coach looks for a way past opponents, combining teamwork with speed.
explanation.definitionFit: To avoid a problem by stepping aside from it is to evade it, finding a route around rather than through.

clue.text: Gesture of respect given late US comic

indicators.note: comic suggests the letters are clowning around and so rearranged

explanation.surface: A tribute is paid to a departed American comedian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'late US comic' reads as a dead comedian; 'comic' is actually an anagram signal for LATE US.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising a hand to the forehead is a formal sign of honour, especially military.

clue.text: Soldier and sailor coming over after leave

indicators.note: after places the sailor's word behind the other piece

parts.note: to desert is to leave or abandon

indicators.note: coming over means turning back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: A soldier and a sailor turn up after going on leave.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the British 7th Armoured Division in the North African campaign, a soldier of WW2.

clue.text: Clear, even at the front

parts.note: straight means even or level
forward means at the front, as of a ship's forward part

explanation.surface: A description of something smooth and level towards the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain and easy to understand: an uncomplicated, honest explanation is clear.

clue.text: Stone me, 'arbinger's outside

indicators.note: outside means the herald word goes around the other piece

parts.note: a harbinger is a herald; the dropped H of the clue says drop it from that word too

explanation.surface: A Cockney exclaims 'Stone me!' to find the messenger waiting outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stone me' looks like an exclamation. The apostrophe in 'arbinger asks for the Cockney dropped H, so herald becomes 'ERALD.
explanation.definitionFit: A green precious gem is a type of stone.

clue.text: A launch at sea

parts.note: to float a company is to launch it on the stock market

explanation.surface: Someone describes a boat being put into the water and taken out on the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'launch' looks nautical but works in its business sense: floating shares on the market.
explanation.definitionFit: Something drifting on the water, not sinking, is buoyant and out on the waves.

clue.text: Educational establishment getting shot of coach

parts.note: getting shot of means getting rid of, finishing with something
to school someone is to coach or train them

explanation.surface: A college dismisses its coach.
explanation.definitionFit: A private college where young women were taught social graces is a type of educational institution.

clue.text: Rebuilt Loire college

indicators.note: rebuilt means the letters are reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: A college rebuilt in France's Loire valley.
explanation.walkthrough: Oriel is one of the colleges of Oxford University.
explanation.definitionFit: A specific Oxford institution is an example of a college.

clue.text: Generate changes in youth

indicators.note: changes says the letters are altered into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Each generation brings changes in young people.
explanation.definitionFit: A young person aged thirteen to nineteen is a youth.

clue.text: Maintenance at an end? On hold

parts.note: up means at an end, as in 'time is up'
to keep something is to hold or retain it

explanation.surface: A repair is completed but then put on hold.
explanation.definitionFit: The cost or process of keeping something in good order is its upkeep: a straight synonym of maintenance.

clue.text: Failure in comic roles

indicators.note: comic suggests the letters are played about with for laughs, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: An actor flops when cast in funny parts.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who keeps failing is commonly called this, the opposite of a winner.

clue.text: Dear old partner deep in thought

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner
pensive means lost in thought, reflective

explanation.surface: A letter opens 'Dear old partner' and the writer is lost in reflection about them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dear' looks like a letter's greeting or a term of affection but means costly.
explanation.definitionFit: Dear in the sense of high-priced: a costly item is one that costs a lot.

clue.text: Period at home at end of the close

parts.note: a term is a period of time, as in a school term
in means at home, as in 'staying in'

indicators.note: the end of the word 'the' is its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone spends a spell at home as the day draws to a close.
explanation.definitionFit: To close something down is to end it or bring it to a stop: verb synonyms.

clue.text: Saucy Latin American dance?

parts.note: a lively Latin American dance that shares its name with a spicy tomato sauce, hence 'saucy'

explanation.surface: A cheeky, flirtatious dance from South or Central America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saucy' looks like it means cheeky but is meant literally: the dance is also a sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin dance and the Mexican-style relish have the same name, so it is a dance that is, punningly, a sauce.

clue.text: Gold coin originally concealed in plant

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the word coin

parts.note: hid means concealed, past tense of hide

explanation.surface: A gold coin was hidden inside a pot plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A flowering plant of a large family prized for its showy blooms is an example of a plant.

clue.text: Archbishop, strictly formal, dined

parts.note: prim means stiffly formal and proper
ate means dined

explanation.surface: A senior churchman ate a stiff, formal dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Archbishop' might lead to an ape, but it is the church title: the Archbishop of Canterbury is Primate of All England.
explanation.definitionFit: The chief bishop of a province carries this title, so an archbishop is one.

clue.text: Group of stars with artist holding protest march up

parts.note: and means with, joining two things

indicators.note: holding means the artist's letters contain another piece

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read upwards, in reverse

parts.note: a demo is a protest march

explanation.surface: Stargazers and an artist take part in a protest march.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, for Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist; in a down clue 'up' reads the march word from the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: A northern constellation named for the princess of Greek myth is a group of stars.

clue.text: Clash between boxers? A scrap that's up in the air

definitions.meaning: a fight between dogs, with boxers taken as the dog breed

definitions.text: A scrap that's up in the air
definitions.meaning: an aerial battle between fighter planes

explanation.surface: A boxing match brawl becomes chaotic and uncertain.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a fight between dogs and close combat between aircraft.

clue.text: Eliminated in match following away round

indicators.note: following says the word for match comes after the other pieces

parts.note: out means away, as in 'she is out'
O is round in shape
fit means match, as in clothes that fit

explanation.surface: A team knocked out of a match after an away game.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: someone no longer in the contest or game has been knocked out of it.

clue.text: Fashionable? Not at university, until now

indicators.note: not tells us to drop the university word from the longer phrase

parts.note: up-to-date means fashionable and current
up means at university, as in 'up at Oxford'

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether being fashionable means having never gone to university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at university' is UP in British usage: students go up to Oxford or Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: So far, up to the present time: two phrases meaning the same.

clue.text: Father describing a deity in temple

indicators.note: describing in its old sense of drawing around, so one piece goes round another

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father
a god is a deity

explanation.surface: Dad tells about a god worshipped in a temple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describing' looks like telling about, but in crosswords it can mean drawing a line around, as a compass describes a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiered tower used as a Buddhist or Hindu shrine is a kind of temple.

clue.text: Complete textbook, superb

definitions.meaning: complete means absolute, total, as in a total stranger
textbook as an adjective means exemplary, ideal

explanation.surface: A reviewer praises a finished textbook as superb.
explanation.definitionFit: The word can mean total, model-exact and excellent, covering all three senses.

clue.text: Type of ring, by the sound of it, for an aquatic bird

indicators.note: by the sound of it signals that the word is said aloud and spelled differently

parts.note: a signet is a kind of finger ring bearing a seal

explanation.surface: A ring takes its name from an aquatic bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A young swan is a water bird, hence an aquatic one.

clue.text: Natural talent shown by lad, at first, in market

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a fair is a market, as in a trade fair

indicators.note: at first selects the opening letter of the word lad

explanation.surface: A young boy shows a gift for selling at a market.
explanation.definitionFit: An instinctive aptitude or knack for something is a gift you were born with.

clue.text: Conscious of a conflict close to home

parts.note: war is a conflict

indicators.note: close to means the final letter of the word home

explanation.surface: Someone is mindful of a war being fought near their home.
explanation.definitionFit: Being mindful or cognisant of something means you know of it.

clue.text: Amateur work involving clergyman in phone book?

indicators.note: involving in the sense of enclosing, so one piece wraps around another

parts.note: DIY, do-it-yourself, is home improvement work done by amateurs
a rector is a parish priest

explanation.surface: A vicar's amateur project appears in the telephone listings.
explanation.definitionFit: A listing of names with numbers is an example of this kind of reference book, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Ten urge AA, after repair, to provide warranty

indicators.note: after repair implies the letters have been fixed and put back in a new order

explanation.surface: A motorist begs the AA breakdown service, ten times over, to stand behind its repairs with a promise.
explanation.walkthrough: The AA is the Automobile Association, a British motoring and breakdown organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: To formally promise that a product will work or be fixed is to give a warranty on it.

clue.text: Large sea duck can, coming across first of eiders

parts.note: a duck is a score of zero in cricket, written O

indicators.note: coming across means spanning, so one word straddles a letter
first of picks the opening letter of the word eiders

explanation.surface: Large sea ducks gather around a tin can floating among eiders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Large sea duck' reads as a bird name, but the definition stops at 'sea'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Atlantic or Pacific are vast bodies of salt water, much bigger than an ordinary sea.

clue.text: Go round close, fashionable

indicators.note: round means surrounding, one piece wrapping another

parts.note: a go is a try or attempt
the close of something is its end

explanation.surface: Someone takes a walk around the stylish neighbourhood close.
explanation.definitionFit: Up-to-the-minute and stylish things are in vogue, so modish in the current way.

clue.text: Faithful wife in LA engrossed by celebrity beginning to talk

indicators.note: engrossed by means absorbed inside another word

parts.note: a star is a celebrity

indicators.note: in places one letter inside two others
beginning to selects the opening letter of the word talk

explanation.surface: A loyal wife in Los Angeles is captivated by a star who starts chatting.
explanation.definitionFit: A dependable, loyal supporter is steadfast and staunch, the meaning of faithful here.
